questions.question: Which dance style was recognised by the famous 'Tanjore Quartet' of the nineteenth century?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest classical dance forms of **India** and is believed to have originated in **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The **Tanjore Quartet**, comprising four brothers—**Chinnayya, Ponnayya, Sivanandam, and Vadivelu**—were instrumental in codifying and organizing Bharatanatyam in the 19th century.
 
• They were musicians, composers, and dance teachers who worked under the patronage of the **Maratha rulers** of Thanjavur (Tanjore).
 
• The Tanjore Quartet systematized the structure of Bharatanatyam performances into the traditional **Margam**, which includes sections like **Alarippu, Jathiswaram, Varnam, Padam, and Thillana.**
 
• Bharatanatyam is deeply rooted in religious and spiritual themes and is often dedicated to **Hindu deities**, especially **Lord Shiva** (Nataraja).
 
• This dance form is known for its intricate footwork, graceful expressions, and strong emphasis on **abhinaya** (expressive acting).
 
• The name Bharatanatyam is derived from the combination of **‘Bhava’ (expression), ‘Raga’ (melody), ‘Tala’ (rhythm), and ‘Natyam’ (dramatic art).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kathakali**__

 __
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance form from **Kerala**, known for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and storytelling.
 
• It is performed as a combination of **dance, drama, and music**, often depicting stories from the **Ramayana and Mahabharata.**
 
• Kathakali performers use intricate hand gestures and facial expressions to convey emotions.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**__
 __
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form originating from **North India**, primarily associated with **storytelling through dance.**
 
• It incorporates intricate footwork, spins, and rhythmic patterns, often accompanied by **Hindustani classical music.**
 
• Kathak evolved in **royal courts** and later incorporated elements of **Mughal culture.**
 
 
 
• **Mohiniattam**__
 
 
• **Mohiniattam** is a classical dance form from **Kerala**, characterized by graceful, feminine movements.
 
• The word **‘Mohini’** refers to the enchanting female form, often associated with the mythology of **Lord Vishnu** as Mohini.
 
• Mohiniattam is performed in **solo** and is set to **Carnatic music.**

questions.question: How much was the literacy rate of India as per census 1951?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**0.1833**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Census of 1951**, the literacy rate in India was recorded as **18.33%**, which corresponds to the value **0.1833** in decimal form.
 
• The 1951 census was the first census conducted in independent India, and it provided crucial insights into the country's **demographic and socio-economic conditions**.
 
• The literacy rate is calculated as the percentage of people aged seven and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• The literacy rate of 18.33% highlighted the challenges in education and marked the beginning of efforts to improve literacy under the **Five-Year Plans** and other government initiatives.
 
• The 1951 census also emphasized the need for policies to enhance education access, particularly in rural and underprivileged areas.
 
• Post-independence, India saw the establishment of institutions like **NCERT (National Council of Educational Research and Training)** and the implementation of schemes like **Operation Blackboard**, aimed at improving educational infrastructure.
 
• The literacy rate serves as a fundamental indicator of a country's development and is closely tied to **economic growth, social progress, and empowerment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Characteristics of Literacy Rate in India**__

 
 
• **Pre-Independence Period:** Literacy rates were extremely low during British rule due to lack of focus on mass education and emphasis on elite institutions.
 
• **Post-1951 Developments:** Efforts to improve literacy included programs like **Adult Literacy Campaigns**, **Mid-Day Meal Scheme**, and **Right to Education Act (2009)**.
 
• **Regional Variations:** States like Kerala have achieved high literacy rates due to strong educational policies, while some states still face challenges in improving literacy.

• His work laid the foundation for the fusion of **Indian and Western music styles**, influencing genres such as jazz, rock, and world music.

questions.question: Which of the following is the least likely to cause obesity in humans?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Over consumption of green vegetables**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Green vegetables** are low in **calories** and high in essential **nutrients**, making them an unlikely cause of obesity.
 
• They are rich in **dietary fiber**, which promotes a feeling of fullness and helps prevent overeating.
 
• Green vegetables contain high amounts of **vitamins**, **minerals**, and **antioxidants**, which contribute to overall health without adding excessive calories.
 
• Common examples of green vegetables include **spinach**, **broccoli**, **kale**, and **lettuce**, all of which are widely recognized as healthy food choices.
 
• Consuming green vegetables as part of a balanced diet can help in weight management and reduce the risk of **chronic diseases** such as heart disease and diabetes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sedentary lifestyle**__

 __
 
• A **sedentary lifestyle** involves minimal physical activity and is a major risk factor for obesity.
 
• Lack of exercise leads to reduced **caloric expenditure**, causing excess calories to be stored as fat.
 
• It is associated with an increased risk of **cardiovascular diseases**, **diabetes**, and **mental health issues**.
 
 
 
• **Genetic traits**__
 __
 
• Obesity can be influenced by **genetic factors**, such as inherited tendencies to store fat or have slower metabolism.
 
• Specific **gene mutations**, like those affecting leptin production or sensitivity, can contribute to weight gain.
 
• While genetics play a role, lifestyle factors can modify their impact on obesity.
 
 
 
• **Over consumption of fat**__
 
 
• Excessive intake of foods rich in **saturated fats** and **trans fats** significantly contributes to obesity.
 
• Fat is high in **calories**, and overconsumption leads to an energy surplus stored as body fat.
 
• Foods like **fried items**, **processed snacks**, and **desserts** are commonly associated with weight gain.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India emphasises the provision of just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 42**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 42** of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• This article directs the State to ensure the provision of **just and humane conditions of work** and **maternity relief.**
 
• The aim is to protect the rights and welfare of workers, particularly women, and promote social justice in the workplace.
 
• **Maternity relief** is vital to safeguard the health and well-being of mothers and newborns, ensuring that women are not disadvantaged due to pregnancy or childbirth.
 
• The inclusion of humane working conditions reflects the commitment of the Constitution to uphold **dignity, equality, and fairness** for all citizens.
 
• This article embodies the idea of a welfare state, focusing on the betterment of citizens' living and working standards.
 
• Though not enforceable by courts, the Directive Principles guide the State in formulating policies and laws to achieve constitutional goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 39**__

 __
 
• **Article 39** relates to the Directive Principles of State Policy and emphasizes the welfare of citizens.
 
• It focuses on securing adequate means of livelihood, ensuring equal pay for equal work, and safeguarding children and youth from exploitation.
 
• It aims to create a fair and equitable society by addressing fundamental inequalities.
 
 
 
• **Article 47**__
 __
 
• **Article 47** directs the State to raise the level of nutrition and standard of living of its people and improve public health.
 
• It emphasizes the prohibition of consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs harmful to health.
 
• This article highlights the importance of a healthy population for the nation's development.
 
 
 
• **Article 44**__
 
 
• **Article 44** relates to the Directive Principles of State Policy and aims to secure a **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)** for all citizens throughout India.
 
• The UCC seeks to replace personal laws based on religion with a common set governing marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption.
 
• This article promotes national integration and equality among citizens.

• It is a **statutory body** formed to address issues related to unfair trade practices, misleading advertisements, and violation of consumer rights.
 
• The CCPA has the authority to investigate complaints, conduct inquiries, and take action against entities violating consumer laws.
 
• In **November 2024**, the CCPA introduced new guidelines focusing on transparency in the **coaching sector**, aiming to regulate practices and safeguard the interests of students.
 
• The guidelines may include provisions for **disclosure of fees**, refund policies, and ensuring ethical advertising practices.
 
• The authority works under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food, and Public Distribution** in India.

questions.question: There are primarily three pieces of equipment, a bowl, a jack and a mat, which are needed to play _____.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Lawn Bowls** is a game that involves rolling balls on a flat lawn or green towards a smaller target ball called the **jack**.
 
• It is played using a **bowl (biased ball)**, a **jack (target ball)**, and a **mat** (used for placement of the bowl).
 
• The game originated in **England** and is popular in several countries such as **Australia, New Zealand, and Canada**.
 
• Lawn Bowls is a sport that requires precision, strategy, and control over the trajectory of the bowl.
 
• The bowls are **weighted or biased** to allow players to curve their trajectory during play.
 
• The objective is to position the bowl as close as possible to the **jack**, outscoring the opponent.
 
• It is played in various formats such as **singles, pairs, triples, and fours**.
 
• Lawn Bowls is included in the **Commonwealth Games** and is recognized as a competitive international sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __

• It is governed by rules to ensure safety, such as **weight classes** and **time limits.**
 
• Boxing originated from ancient combat techniques and gained prominence in modern sports during the **18th century**.
 
• Prominent boxing events include the **Olympics**, **World Championships**, and professional fights organized by bodies such as the **WBC**, **WBA**, and **IBF**.
 
 
 
• **Table Tennis**__
 __
 
• **Table Tennis**, also known as ping pong, is played using a paddle, a lightweight ball, and a table with a net.
 
• The sport was invented in **England** during the late **19th century** and is now popular worldwide.
 
• It requires quick reflexes, precision, and strategy to outscore the opponent by hitting the ball across the net.
 
• Popular international events include the **World Table Tennis Championships** and the **Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Fencing**__
 
 
• **Fencing** is a combat sport that involves sword fighting using weapons such as the **foil**, **épée**, and **sabre**.
 
• The sport originated in **Europe** and dates back to the **Middle Ages**.
 
• It is now a major part of the **Olympics**, with athletes competing in individual and team events.
 
• Fencing requires agility, precision, and strategic movements to score points by striking the opponent.

questions.question: Which of the following sites provides evidence of early urban planning during the Middle Iron Age in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Kausambi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kausambi** is an important archaeological site that provides substantial evidence of **early urban planning** during the **Middle Iron Age in India**.
 
• Located in present-day **Uttar Pradesh**, Kausambi was a significant city in the ancient kingdom of Vatsa.
 
• Excavations at Kausambi have revealed a well-planned city layout with **fortifications, gates, and bastions**, showcasing advanced urban planning techniques.
 
• The site includes remnants of **drainage systems**, indicating a focus on sanitation and organized infrastructure.
 
• Kausambi was an important center of trade and governance, highlighting its role in the **economic and political landscape** of the time.
 
• It is also associated with the **Buddhist tradition**, as it was visited by Gautama Buddha and later became a center of Buddhist learning.
 
• Kausambi's urban planning reflects the transition from rural to organized urban centers during the **Iron Age** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harappa**__

 __
 
• **Harappa** is a major site of the **Indus Valley Civilization**, which predates the Middle Iron Age.
 
• It is located in present-day **Pakistan** and is known for its advanced urban planning, including **grid layouts, drainage systems, and granaries**.
 
• However, it does not belong to the **Middle Iron Age** but to the earlier **Bronze Age (3300–1300 BCE)**.
 
 
 
• **Lothal**__
 __
 
• **Lothal**, located in present-day Gujarat, was another site of the **Indus Valley Civilization**.
 
• It is famous for its **dockyard** and is considered one of the earliest known ports in the world.
 
• Like Harappa, it belongs to the **Bronze Age** and not the **Middle Iron Age**.
 
 
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro**__
 
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro** is one of the most prominent cities of the **Indus Valley Civilization**.
 
• It is located in present-day **Pakistan** and is known for its **Great Bath**, advanced drainage systems, and urban infrastructure.
 
• Similar to Harappa and Lothal, it belongs to the **Bronze Age**, not the Middle Iron Age.

questions.question: From which region of the Himalayas does the river Brahmaputra originate?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Northern**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Brahmaputra River** originates from the **Angsi Glacier** in the northern region of the Himalayas in **Tibet, China.**
 
• It is locally known as the **Yarlung Tsangpo** in Tibet.
 
• The river flows eastward through Tibet, enters India through Arunachal Pradesh, and then flows through Assam and Bangladesh.
 
• The Brahmaputra is one of the largest rivers in the world and is known for its **extreme hydrological variability**, causing floods during the monsoon season.
 
• The river is significant for its **cultural, economic, and ecological importance** in the regions it flows through.
 
• The Brahmaputra merges with the Ganges River in Bangladesh, forming the world's largest delta, the **Sundarbans Delta.**
 
• It supports a rich biodiversity, including species such as the **Gangetic Dolphin** and numerous migratory birds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Southern**__

 __
 
• The term "Southern" does not apply to the origin of the Brahmaputra River as it originates from the **northern Himalayas**.
 
• The Southern Himalayas are primarily known for being home to foothills and valleys like the **Shivalik Hills**, which do not serve as the source for major rivers like the Brahmaputra.
 
 
 
• **Eastern**__
 __
 
• The Brahmaputra flows through Eastern India, but its **source is not located in the Eastern Himalayas**.
 
• The Eastern Himalayas are significant for other rivers like the **Teesta River** and tributaries of the Brahmaputra, but not the main river itself.
 
 
 
• **Western**__
 
 
• The Western Himalayas are the source of rivers like the **Indus River** and its tributaries.
 
• The Brahmaputra does not originate here, as its source is in the **northern region** of the Himalayas.

questions.question: What were the main objectives of the Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79)?

options.text: Removal of poverty and attainment of self-reliance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Removal of poverty and attainment of self-reliance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79)** was launched with the primary goals of achieving **poverty alleviation** (Garibi Hatao) and ensuring **economic self-reliance**.
 
• It emphasized the importance of strengthening the economy to reduce dependence on foreign aid and achieve sustainable development.
 
• The plan was influenced by the **economic challenges** India faced during the early 1970s, including **inflation, food shortages, and energy crises.**
 
• The government focused on implementing programs such as the **Minimum Needs Programme** to address basic needs like health, education, and rural infrastructure.
 
• It also prioritized the creation of **employment opportunities**, particularly in rural areas, to uplift the economically weaker sections of society.
 
• The plan introduced measures for **agricultural and industrial development** aimed at increasing production and ensuring economic stability.
 
• Though the plan was later terminated in 1978 by the **Janata Party government**, its objectives laid the foundation for subsequent poverty reduction strategies in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industrialisation and infrastructure**__

 __
 
• While the Fifth Five-Year Plan did touch upon industrial growth and infrastructure development, these were not the primary objectives.
 
• **Industrialisation** was a key focus of earlier plans, particularly the **Second Five-Year Plan**, which emphasized heavy industries and public sector enterprises.
 
• Infrastructure projects were given importance but were seen as a means to achieve self-reliance and poverty alleviation, rather than standalone goals.
 
 
 
• **Defense and military expansion**__
 __
 
• India's Five-Year Plans primarily focus on economic and social development rather than defense strategies.
 
• Defense and military expansion are addressed through separate budgets and policies outside the scope of Five-Year Plans.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural development and education**__
 
 
• Agricultural development and education were addressed as part of the **Minimum Needs Programme**, but they were not the main focus of the Fifth Plan.
 
• Agriculture was a major focus of the **First Five-Year Plan**, and education gained prominence in later plans as part of human capital development.

questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, which of the following is NOT a power of the Governor?

options.text: Vote during the no confidence motion

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Vote during the no confidence motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor**, as per the Indian Constitution, is the constitutional head of the state and does not participate in the voting during a **no-confidence motion**.
 
• A **no-confidence motion** is a parliamentary motion presented by the legislators questioning the confidence of the ruling government or its policies in the legislature.
 
• Such motions are debated and voted upon in the legislative assembly, where the elected representatives, not the Governor, decide the outcome.
 
• The Governor, being a constitutional authority, does not hold any legislative or executive voting rights in the assembly.
 
• The Governor's role is limited to ensuring the smooth functioning of the state legislature and exercising powers like summoning, proroguing, and dissolving the assembly as per constitutional provisions.
 
• Thus, the Governor cannot vote during a no-confidence motion, which is exclusively a function of the legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Prorogue the state legislature**__

 __
 
• The Governor has the constitutional authority to **prorogue** the state legislature, which means discontinuing a session without dissolving it.
 
• This power is exercised as per **Article 174** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is used to manage legislative sessions and ensure smooth governance.
 
 
 
• **Summon the state legislature**__
 __
 
• The Governor has the power to **summon** the state legislature as per **Article 174** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This involves convening the legislative assembly or council for conducting legislative business.
 
• Summoning is a critical function for initiating legislative processes.
 
 
 
• **Dissolve the state legislature**__
 
 
• The Governor can dissolve the state legislature, particularly the legislative assembly, as per **Article 174**, when necessary, such as in case of a failure to form a government.
 
• Dissolution ends the term of the assembly, leading to elections for a new legislature.
